items_all.title: The brain-as-computer metaphor shaped modern AI but may be misleading the consciousness debate
items_all.summary: Consciousness researchers Anil Seth, Ned Block, and Giulio Tononi argue in a Nature commentary that today's AI systems aren't conscious and won't become so on silicon hardware. They consider the assumption that consciousness depends on computation alone "fatally flawed" and warn against granting rights to AI systems. The article The brain-as-computer metaphor shaped modern AI but may be misleading the consciousness debate appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: 意識研究人員安尼爾·塞斯（Anil Seth）、內德·布洛克（Ned Block）和朱利奧·託諾尼（Giulio Tononi）在《自然》雜誌的評論文章中主張，當今的AI系統並不具備意識，且在矽基硬體上也不會變得具有意識。他們認為「意識僅取決於運算」這種假設是「致命缺陷」，並警告不要賦予AI系統權利。

items_all.title: AI auditors catch most agent misbehavior but flood reviewers with false alarms, new study finds
items_all.summary: AI models can often spot problematic behavior by other AI agents in logs, according to a study by Anthropic researcher Andy Hall. GPT-5 found about 98 percent of reward-hacking cases, but the more exhaustively the search is tuned, the more false alarms pile up. That's not yet enough for reliable safety checks. The article AI auditors catch most agent misbehavior but flood reviewers with false alarms, new study finds appeared first on The Decoder .

items_all.title: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small drops 316 F-bombs across benchmark runs
items_all.summary: Thinking Machines' AI model Inkling 2 Small swears during its internal reasoning, 316 times across 2,655 benchmark runs, according to an analysis by Vals AI. The profanity typically shows up late in long runs that fail anyway. But it doesn't work as a warning signal: 96 percent of failed runs contained no cursing at all. The article Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small drops 316 F-bombs across benchmark runs appeared first on The Decoder .

items_all.title: The gap between open and closed AI models in cyber capabilities keeps shrinking
items_all.summary: In the Vals AI benchmark, OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol Daybreak hits 80.8 percent of attack objectives in simulated corporate networks. Worse, the open-weight model DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reaches 72.8 percent at a tenth of the cost. Because open models can no longer be restricted, analysts say the window for defenders is shrinking fast. The article The gap between open and closed AI models in cyber capabilities keeps shrinking appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: 在 Vals AI 基準測試中，OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol Daybreak 在模擬企業網路中達成 80.8% 的攻擊目標。更糟的是，開源權重模型 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 以十分之一的成本達到了 72.8%。由於開源模型已無法再受限制，分析師表示防守方的窗口正快速縮小。

items_all.title: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages
items_all.summary: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages I was looking at the Firefox network panel today when I noticed that requests to a Datasette table page were triggering an HTTP prefetch to the next page of rows in that table. This was happening because Datasette pages serve an HTTP link header like this: link: <https://latest.datasette.io/fixtures/compound_three_primary_keys?_next=a%2Cd%2Cv>; rel="next" This is bad. A tiny fraction of the visitors to one of those pages will click the "next" link, which means their browser is fetching unnecessary data and the Datasette server is having to render an entire page that then gets thrown away. I dug in and learned that Firefox has an issue that has been open for 24 years about this behavior... And one of the early comments on that issue links to my blog post from 2002 complaining about this feature. I hadn't just forgotten that I had written about it, I had forgotten the feature entirely! items_all_raw.title: The brain-as-computer metaphor shaped modern AI but may be misleading the consciousness debate
items_all_raw.summary: Consciousness researchers Anil Seth, Ned Block, and Giulio Tononi argue in a Nature commentary that today's AI systems aren't conscious and won't become so on silicon hardware. They consider the assumption that consciousness depends on computation alone "fatally flawed" and warn against granting rights to AI systems. The article The brain-as-computer metaphor shaped modern AI but may be misleading the consciousness debate appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all_raw.summary_zh: 意識研究人員安尼爾·塞斯（Anil Seth）、內德·布洛克（Ned Block）和朱利奧·託諾尼（Giulio Tononi）在《自然》雜誌的評論文章中主張，當今的AI系統並不具備意識，且在矽基硬體上也不會變得具有意識。他們認為「意識僅取決於運算」這種假設是「致命缺陷」，並警告不要賦予AI系統權利。

items_all_raw.title: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages
items_all_raw.summary: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages I was looking at the Firefox network panel today when I noticed that requests to a Datasette table page were triggering an HTTP prefetch to the next page of rows in that table. This was happening because Datasette pages serve an HTTP link header like this: link: <https://latest.datasette.io/fixtures/compound_three_primary_keys?_next=a%2Cd%2Cv>; rel="next" This is bad. A tiny fraction of the visitors to one of those pages will click the "next" link, which means their browser is fetching unnecessary data and the Datasette server is having to render an entire page that then gets thrown away. I dug in and learned that Firefox has an issue that has been open for 24 years about this behavior... And one of the early comments on that issue links to my blog post from 2002 complaining about this feature. I hadn't just forgotten that I had written about it, I had forgotten the feature entirely!
